data.narrative:
Red 6, a Series B+ stage defense and security company founded by Daniel Robinson, has raised over $100M to date. The broader Defense & Security sector comprises 21 peer companies across public and private markets, including 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers. Top private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Standard peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints at Red 6's specific stage and valuation tier. Within the 21 same-sector peers identified, zero companies satisfied simultaneous filters for stage alignment, adjacency, or similar valuation scale—the minimum threshold of three datapoints necessary for reliable peer-median triangulation. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of defense technology companies across development stages and go-to-market models.

The analysis exposes a structural constraint common to early-stage frontier defense technology: sparse public market comparables and limited disclosure among private peers at comparable funding levels. Without quantitative triangulation results, this valuation requires either (1) revenue or unit-economic data from Red 6 itself, enabling revenue multiple or DCF approaches, or (2) expansion into adjacent sector comps, with explicit caveats on transferability. The key uncertainty remains whether Red 6's capital intensity and time-to-revenue align more closely with pure software, systems integration, or hardware-dominant defense contractors.
